objections.title: An existential warning escape is not yet the policy escape
objections.failure_trace_or_prerequisite: The issuer can admit a zone/time pair because some named authored escape segment is affordable. All three policies respond to any LETHAL_WARNING using their one ESCAPE route. The written interface does not bind the selected warning witness to that route or expose a named witness identifier. The encounters assume no lethal warning during their unusual-operation traces, so they do not supply this binding by example. This leaves controller/issuer compatibility unshown; it does not make the world reachability obligation internally impossible.

evidence.rationale: Issuer asks for at least one authored witness.
C02 always emits its named ESCAPE.
C04 always emits its named ESCAPE while debt remains compulsory.
C06 always emits its named ESCAPE.
Authored examples expressly do not prove arbitrary compatibility.

objections.required_to_close: Name the finite issuer-to-policy route binding or constrain the example warning to the actual authored ESCAPE, and give one compatible commitment/warning trace. Keep earlier cast/debt/edit costs and motion intact. Do not add a hidden route optimizer or promise that every voluntary later action preserves the escape.
objections.claim_ceiling: Written reasoning only; no executed failure or impossibility claim.

objections.title: Event-gated route progress needs a retained cursor contract
objections.failure_trace_or_prerequisite: PREP_LOOP has interruption and cast-admission gates, but higher rules issue STOP, CANCEL and MOVE(EXIT). The common contract says movement requests can replace one another. It does not state whether reissuing PREP_LOOP resumes its retained waypoint or restarts, or whether a mark/admission gate occurring while another movement command owns the channel advances the loop. The authored example can work if the right cursor/latch semantics are chosen; those semantics are not yet named.

evidence.rationale: Replacement, stop and continuation are explicit but cursor lifetime is not.
Arrival advances a route waypoint; wait events are fixed gates.
PREP_LOOP must retain progress through interruption/admission waits.
CANCEL issues STOP while funding a real mark.
Reissues a route after higher-priority action/EXIT ownership.

objections.required_to_close: Declare one finite route-cursor owner, event-gate identity/consumption and same-route resume/restart behavior. Show P1 interruption→P2 and H admission→EXIT→loop resumption with those exact semantics. Preserve real failed casts and actual outward crossings; no geometric route search.
objections.claim_ceiling: Written reasoning only; no executed failure or impossibility claim.

objections.title: The ordinary fallback has not been connected to its attack pad
objections.failure_trace_or_prerequisite: Once PREPARATION and REGION_ACTIVE are false, rule 6 selects PERIMETER and allows ATTACK only at M. Rule 5 also permits ordinary casts only during preparation or at H with a region. M is defined as a PREP_LOOP node, while PERIMETER is not given a route or an M arrival. Thus the current six-rule witness does not show ordinary offense for the promised no-tool/later-no-refill branch. A perimeter through M could close it; the present text does not establish such a route.

evidence.rationale: M belongs to the preparation loop; PERIMETER is not defined here.
Ordinary cast admission is gated by preparation or active region.
PERIMETER fallback still restricts attacks to M.
Promises ordinary hero plans without the tool.
Later stages have no mandatory residue bundle.

objections.required_to_close: Connect the same six-rule policy to an explicit ordinary route and legal attack/cast window when no tool/credits/region are available, or clearly give the separate six-rule ordinary policy selected at a pause. Do not count a hidden hero strategy manager as the fallback.
objections.claim_ceiling: Written reasoning only; no executed failure or impossibility claim.

objections.title: Armed-window expiry and hit capture have an unnamed tie
objections.failure_trace_or_prerequisite: ARM creates a two-second window. At exactly its deadline a qualifying direct hit resolves damage and asks whether the living hero is armed. The event order defines damage, capture and debt timeout, but never places arm expiry or states a strict deadline comparison. Capture versus immediate ordinary knockback therefore has no unique written result in a named state. This is a missing branch, not an observed double settlement.

evidence.rationale: Sets the two-second armed window and nonrefundable cost.
Capture depends on armed state.
Contains debt timeout ordering but no armed-window expiration.

objections.required_to_close: State the exact armed eligibility interval and its expiration owner/order relative to same-boundary damage, capture and newly admitted arm requests. Preserve normal HP loss, one paid arm and one eventual debt settlement when capture is eligible.
objections.claim_ceiling: Written reasoning only; no executed failure or impossibility claim.

objections.title: Arming does not itself hold the receiving pad
objections.failure_trace_or_prerequisite: After ARM is admitted, rule 5 becomes false because ARMED is true. With no debt yet, rule 6 emits PERIMETER movement and ordinary offense. The example assumes the qualifying hit occurs at A, but neither the hit time relative to the 0.2-second recovery nor the armed portion of PERIMETER is specified. This could be compatible if the hit lands during recovery or on a declared route segment; the saved policy does not show that choice.

evidence.rationale: ARM branch applies only while NOT ARMED.
Armed/no-debt falls to perimeter and offense.
The HOLD_ROUTE witness begins from A after capture.
Assumes a hit at A within the window without controller timing.

objections.required_to_close: Provide an explicit armed/no-debt movement/admission trace that receives or deliberately declines the qualifying hit under the same six rules. State its ordinary hit reserve and prior-action behavior; do not silently freeze the hero or supply a free guard.
objections.claim_ceiling: Written reasoning only; no executed failure or impossibility claim.

objections.title: Gate admission can coincide with route-deadline return
objections.failure_trace_or_prerequisite: A scout waits at closed WEST until its six-second commitment deadline. Another actor crosses NORTH exactly at that deadline, opening WEST. Event order processes gate passage admission before closing the commitment deadline. The admitted passage lasts 0.5 seconds, but the deadline branch immediately starts fixed RETURN. The contract does not say which movement owns the scout until the admitted passage completes or when return/read timing begins. Choosing a transition can close this branch; both must not move it independently.

evidence.rationale: An admitted gate passage is a 0.5-second committed action.
Deadline aborts remaining route and begins RETURN.
Gate admissions precede commitment deadline closure.

objections.required_to_close: Assign one owner and explicit precedence for deadline-time gate admission, already admitted passage and RETURN initiation. Include the same-boundary third-party opening case. Retain current-law passage checks and the acquired stale route; no teleport, retroactive gate denial or duplicate move.
objections.claim_ceiling: Written reasoning only; no executed failure or impossibility claim.

objections.title: A blocked return has no stated arrival-to-read disposition
objections.failure_trace_or_prerequisite: The scout can fail before WEST or wait there, yet RETURN is described as one fixed two-second path to P. The text acknowledges obstructed source travel but does not define return from each interrupted route location, stopping on a blocked return, or READ eligibility after failed physical return. The full invariant should require an actual P arrival; a fixed elapsed time alone must not refresh the acquired version remotely. This is a bounded lifecycle omission rather than a demand for general pathfinding.

evidence.rationale: READ occurs at P.
Return is fixed and nominally two seconds.
Obstruction can delay source travel.
Ordinary authored routes stop and expose obstruction.

objections.required_to_close: Declare fixed return segments/starting states for the finite route table, obstruction wait/stop behavior and actual arrival as the READ precondition. Distinguish a two-second clear-path fixture from a universal return guarantee; do not invent a shortest-path search.
objections.claim_ceiling: Written reasoning only; no executed failure or impossibility claim.

objections.title: The USE branch lacks a stated lawful history to NORTH
objections.failure_trace_or_prerequisite: Every phase initializes EAST. Only DENY_PLAN admits AMEND(NORTH), while rule 5 needs USE_PLAN and current NORTH. The plan is selected at setup or a pause. A setup USE plan cannot itself produce that state. A later lawful pause/handover after a DENY amendment might, but the required history is not shown. Preserving EAST is a valid alternative already; intentional current-NORTH use should be bounded by its actual reachable precondition.

evidence.rationale: Phase begins at EAST.
DENY or USE is chosen at setup or paused selection.
Only DENY branch issues AMEND.
USE requires NORTH and a waiting scout.
Claims intentional opening of current NORTH as an alternative.

objections.required_to_close: Supply a legal history for the NORTH/USE state using declared controller handover/paused plan selection, or limit the supplied auto alternative to preserving EAST and mark NORTH-use as manual/conditional. No automatic midcombat usefulness selector is needed.
objections.claim_ceiling: Written reasoning only; no executed failure or impossibility claim.
